rationale: This is a tiny (196 lines, 16 functions, ~1.7 KB text) C++ symbolic-differentiation benchmark whose core logic is class-polymorphic (quotient_expr/prod_expr/sum_expr::deriv) with one dominant function (main, 558 B), so control-flow obfuscation on the larger functions and virtual-dispatch/call indirection give the best resistance-per-byte. FLA gets the highest security/diversity weights because flattening main and the deriv methods destroys the readable recursive structure, and SUB plus SPLIT are weighted generously since they are near-free in runtime and size and compound strongly with flattening; IGV and ICALL are weighted to target the C++ vtable/virtual-call surface that a reverse engineer would pivot on, with moderate cost weights since the program is call-dense relative to its size; BCF is kept at moderate weights because its bogus-block blowup is disproportionately expensive on a 1.7 KB text segment; IBR sits in the middle as a complementary branch-hiding transform; and CorrectnessRisk weights are held low-to-moderate across all passes (highest for ICALL/IGV, which rewrite call and global-reference semantics in C++ code) to preserve correctness on this correctly-behaving reference binary.
